paras: The Clarksville circus tent shooting was the killing of an unnamed Black man by Deputy Sheriff John Stephens inside a crowded circus tent at Clarksville, Texas, on October 30, 1903. According to the only report found, the man, described as drunk, shot the deputy first and was killed instantly when Stephens returned fire.

A circus was in progress at Clarksville on October 30 when, according to a special dispatch to The St. Louis Republic, Stephens was shot in the tent by a man the paper called "a drunken negro." Stephens returned the fire and killed the man instantly. The tent was crowded and "the wildest excitement prevailed," but the dispatch said no one else was hurt. The extent of the deputy's wound was not reported, and the dead man was not named.
No report of an inquest, an investigation of the shooting or any later follow-up appears in the coverage found.

The St. Louis Republic was the only paper found to carry the story, running it twice in its issue of October 31, 1903. On page six it printed the special under the headline "Killing Under Circus Tent. Negro Attacked Officer and Was Shot to Death," giving the deputy's name and the date. Its page-one "General Domestic" digest condensed the item to a single line saying the man "attacked a Deputy Sheriff" and "was shot to death before a large crowd."

Both items identified the dead man only as "a drunken negro" and presented the officer's version as fact, with no account from witnesses or from the man's side. No coverage of the shooting was found in the Black press.

accounts.label: Republic special from Clarksville
accounts.gist: The man, drunk, shot Deputy Stephens in the circus tent; Stephens returned fire and killed him instantly, and no one else in the crowded tent was hurt. Only this version, which puts the first shot on the dead man, appears.

accounts.label: Republic news digest
accounts.gist: A 'drunken negro' attacked a deputy sheriff during a circus and was 'shot to death before a large crowd.'

framing.detail: The Republic headlined 'Negro Attacked Officer and Was Shot to Death', called the man 'a drunken negro' and gave only the deputy's side, treating the killing as return fire.

record_check.record: The date is not given beyond the issue date.
record_check.dossier: The special is datelined Clarksville, Tex., Oct. 30 and says 'to-day', so the event date is October 30, 1903.
The deputy was reported shot; his race is not stated and the extent of the wound is not given.
Neither article names the county; only 'Clarksville, Tex.' is given.
Single source: two items in one issue of one paper, the digest line derived from the special.

record_check.record: attacked a Deputy Sheriff during the progress of a circus
record_check.dossier: The fuller report says the man shot the deputy first; this comes only from the officer's side via the Republic special.
